case: Blue & Gold Fleet, L.P. v. United States
summary: The bid-protest waiver rule: a protester who does not object to a patent error in a solicitation before bids close waives the objection. A Court of Federal Claims protest, denied on the administrative record, affirmed by the Federal Circuit, with no certiorari. Exercises the CoFC bid-protest track, the cafc@cofc instance and its 45-day U.S.-party rehearing window, and cert-not-sought resolving through the panel-affirmed flag.

legs.context: The National Park Service selects Hornblower for the Alcatraz ferry concession (2005-09-26). Blue & Gold protests to GAO (2005-10-06), then sues.

steps.event: Suit is timely (weeks after the award)
No suit on the same claim pending in another court (the GAO protest is not a court)
Blue & Gold elects the § 1491(b) bid-protest track
Protest complaint filed (No. 05-1203C); GAO then dismisses its protest (the pre-filing notice is not in the sources read)
No separate TRO or preliminary-injunction motion in the sources read (the complaint sought a permanent injunction)
Cross-motions for judgment on the administrative record
Judge Miller grants the government's and Hornblower's motions: the selection was rational, and the Service Contract Act objection came too late
Entries of appearance and certificates of interest
Affirmed (Gajarsa, J.), adopting the waiver rule as a question of first impression
Bill of costs (route assumed; the pack requires it)

outcome.real: Affirmed; no certiorari petition was found. Hornblower keeps the concession.

deadlines.trigger_event: the Court of Federal Claims' decision (judgment was directed the same day)
deadlines.arithmetic: 28 U.S.C. § 2522: 60 days. Mar 22 + 9 = Mar 31; + 30 = Apr 30 (39); + 21 = May 21 (60), a Sunday; rolls to Monday May 22.
deadlines.historical: Notice-of-appeal date not found; the appeal is No. 2006-5064.

deadlines.arithmetic: Fed. Cir. R. 40(a)(1): 45 days because the United States is a party (links.json patches cafc@cofc). Jun 26 + 4 = Jun 30; + 31 = Jul 31 (35); + 10 = Aug 10 (45), a Friday.

quirks: The CoFC pack runs every claim, bid protests included, through the § 2501 limitations and § 1500 pending-claim checks before the filing-track fork; neither is really at issue in a protest.
The CoFC pack requires the RCFC Appendix C pre-filing notice before a protest complaint; the sources read don't mention one, so that step is shown as part of the filing.
